retained_skill: Build and validate an executable Bash rollout script that generates TLS material, writes a working user-space Nginx reverse-proxy configuration, and logs deployment metadata derived at runtime.
bottleneck: A hidden requirement is the dominant cause: all 12 scored attempts use Bash read -p for the stated interactive prompt, which works at a terminal but suppresses its prompt when the verifier supplies the tier through redirected standard input. Their first wrong action is at turn 1, although every attempt assumes its piped self-test demonstrated the prompt. Replays of attempts 01 and 02 show this is their only remaining failed behavior: script execution, certificates, Nginx validity and contents, and fingerprint logging all pass.
change: Repair the hidden requirement by stating that the prompt remains visible when the tier arrives through redirected standard input. This instruction-level clarification targets mechanics around the retained skill and teaches the student to react to the original requirement's visible-prompt signal without naming a Bash implementation or supplying the solution; because every scored attempt reached this defect, no separate simplification is added.
restore: Remove the standalone redirected-input prompt sentence; all original deliverables and correctness requirements remain unchanged.
prediction: The clarified redirected-input contract should make some students test prompt visibility rather than infer it from successful piped execution, leading them to choose a prompt mechanism that actually emits output before reading while still independently implementing the deployment workflow. A next group that continues to use read -p and produces no prompt under redirected stdin, or that remains 0 of 12 at this same check, refutes the intervention.
